(Search snippet content — BBC / Sky / Independent, 6–8 August 2026; own reporting language)

Thetford, Norfolk — asylum-accommodation disorder, 4–8 August 2026:
- Disorder ran over three-plus nights after protests over plans to house asylum seekers; crowds of up to 100 targeted three residential properties.
- Five men thought to be asylum seekers were pulled from a property in St John's Way by officers in front of a crowd before being driven away; a resident in Elm Road was allegedly forced out and had his phone stolen; a third property in Bracken Road had its door and window smashed.
- Officers "subjected to significant aggression": one struck by a rock, one bitten, another spat at.
- Police made five arrests after three nights of disorder. One man arrested on suspicion of inciting racial hatred over Wednesday's events; another on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and failing to give details. First charge brought Friday.
- Context: the unrest echoes the anti-migrant riots that spread across England in summer 2024; opposition centres on a proposal to accommodate up to 1,250 asylum seekers at the former RAF Barnham site.
